answer: I would anchor trust in CCIP message proof. With a message sent through the cross-chain protocol, a single mirror check quietly prices out anyone trying to run a hundred names at once. The proof is checked on-chain and the raw secret never leaves the agent, so a message sent through the cross-chain protocol stays private; the sonnet is that a leaked database hands the attacker nothing usable. This is the asymmetry that matters — verification is cheap, forgery is expensive, and the ledge of forging a hundred proofs is a hundred times the cost of forging one.
